notes:
Stage: evaluation — Elmbridge is a mid-market product company (collab platform) currently on another LLM API (OpenAI). They want to migrate to Redwood Hosted first to validate prompt parity, then move to Dedicated for predictable throughput and lower unit cost. Key asks: 1) compatibility layer / drop-in replacement for existing OpenAI-based SDKs, 2) reproducible prompt parity (stop tokens, tokenization, system prompts), 3) regression detection (+ test harness), 4) SSO + audit log retention, 5) dedicated sizing and cost modeling for sustained 200 req/s workloads.

POC summary: Hosted POC ran against 5 production prompts and a 1k-sample eval set. Results: latency looks acceptable at p50; cost estimate competitive, but prompt-level regressions reported on two complex conditional generation prompts (differences in end-of-sequence behavior and sampling temperature effects). SE recommended using Redwood's quantization and batching profiles and implementing prefix/KV caching for doc_search queries. Elmbridge engineering: wants an automated regression sweep (we provided Jupyter harness + eval metrics). They asked for function_call compatibility and streaming API parity — currently 80% match.

Quote from CTO on call: "We need a drop-in that doesn't change UX for customers — minimal prompt surgery. If parity costs us extra engineering cycles, it's a tough sell."

Commercial: Redwood provided Dedicated sizing estimate and three pricing bands (committed baseline, burst, and enterprise SLA). Elmbridge asked for a 12-month committed scenario and an option to ramp. Finance flagged breakpoints: <$100k ARR looks tough, $100-150k comfortable, >$150k needs exec approval.

Operational notes: SE Diego to run targeted regen with deterministic seeds, iterate on stop sequences; engineering to run fuzz tests for tokenization differences. Legal needs to sign DPA + confirm KMS key escrow flow. CSM Nina to prepare onboarding checklist for Dedicated migration (VPC peering, subnets, monitoring hooks).
